drills.q: What does the oxide in a MOSFET do?
options: It insulates the gate from the silicon, so no current flows through the gate
It conducts current from the gate into the channel
It protects the silicon from contamination during manufacture
It sets the threshold voltage
drills.why: The gate is not connected to what it controls. That is the structural fact every convenient property of CMOS logic follows from, and it is why one gate can drive another at no static cost.

drills.q: With the gate at zero volts, why does no current flow from source to drain?
options: The channel has too much resistance
The path crosses two junctions back to back, and one of them blocks
The oxide blocks it
The source and drain are not connected to anything
drills.why: Two islands of one doping in a body of the other make two junctions in series facing opposite ways. There is no direction you can push that both will allow.

options: The gate voltage at which the surface of the body inverts and a channel forms
The maximum voltage the gate can take before the oxide breaks down
The voltage across the channel when the transistor is on
The supply voltage of the circuit
drills.why: Below it, no bridge. Above it, a bridge. It is the voltage at which the gate's field has pulled enough minority carriers to the surface that the surface behaves like the islands on either side of it.

drills.q: Below the threshold voltage, the drain current is:
options: Exactly zero
Small and falling exponentially, never reaching zero
Constant at a small value set by the process
Rising, but too slowly to matter
drills.why: This is the whole difficulty. The switch does not open, it becomes very resistive, and how quickly it does that is measured in millivolts of gate voltage per decade of current.

drills.q: What sets the floor on the subthreshold slope?
options: Thermal energy divided by charge, so it is physics rather than
The thickness of the gate oxide
The purity of the silicon
The width of the transistor
drills.why: It is kT/q times the natural log of ten, about 60 millivolts per decade at room temperature. No process improvement moves it, which is why the responses have all been structural.

drills.q: At 60 mV per decade, lowering the threshold by 100 mV multiplies off-current by roughly:
drills.why: A hundred divided by sixty is 1.67 decades, and ten to that is about 46. Computing this is the second exercise, and the number is why lowering the supply voltage stopped being possible.

drills.q: An NMOS transistor passes which level cleanly?
options: A low
A high
Both equally
Neither, without a pull-up resistor
drills.why: Trying to pass a high, its source terminal rises with the output, so its own gate-to-source voltage falls, and it shuts itself off a threshold short of the supply.

drills.q: Why are pull-up networks built from PMOS rather than NMOS?
options: PMOS is faster
It is a convention inherited from older logic families
An NMOS pull-up cannot deliver a full high, because it turns itself off
PMOS uses less area
drills.why: It is the transistor refusing rather than a designer choosing. PMOS is in fact the slower of the two, and it is used for pull-up anyway because it is the one that can finish the job.

drills.q: Why must a PMOS transistor be made wider than an NMOS one for the same drive?
options: Its carriers move more slowly, so it needs more width to pass the same current
It has a higher threshold voltage
Its oxide is thicker
To balance the layout visually
drills.why: And a wider transistor presents more capacitance to whatever drives it, so stacking PMOS in series costs twice: once in speed and once in load. That is the fact that makes NAND cheap and AND expensive.

drills.q: Charging a gate capacitance to V and discharging it again takes about:
options: C*V
C*V*V
C*V*V/2
V*V/C
drills.why: The supply moves a charge of C*V through a drop of V. Half of that ends up stored in the capacitor and the other half is dissipated in the transistor doing the charging, which is why the stored energy is half the delivered energy.

drills.q: Why did gate oxide tunnelling force a change of material?
options: At about a nanometre the insulator was five atoms thick and electrons
Silicon dioxide melts at the temperatures modern chips reach
Thinner oxide made the threshold voltage unstable
The material was too expensive at scale
drills.why: A physically thicker layer of a higher dielectric constant gives the same capacitance with far less tunnelling. The switch to hafnium oxide with a metal gate is a leakage fix, not a speed improvement.

drills.q: The fin, and later the gate wrapped around the channel, exist mainly to:
options: Increase drive current
Give the gate more control of the channel so the transistor turns off properly
Reduce manufacturing cost
Allow higher supply voltages
drills.why: All of the structural changes since 45 nm are about restoring electrostatic control. They improve speed as a side effect and they were adopted because transistors had stopped switching off.

options: Leakage rises with temperature, and leakage is power, which raises
Leakage falls with temperature as carriers scatter more
They are independent
Leakage rises only above the rated junction temperature
drills.why: It is a feedback loop. Within what the package can remove it settles at some temperature. Outside that, it does not settle.

drills.q: First-order, the propagation delay of a gate is proportional to:
options: Its width
Its on-resistance times the capacitance it drives
The supply voltage
The number of inputs it has
drills.why: About ln(2) times R times C, to the halfway point. Making a transistor wider lowers its resistance and raises the capacitance it presents, so speed moves from this gate to the one driving it.

drills.q: Static power is different from dynamic power because:
options: It is larger
It is spent whether or not the chip is doing any work
It depends on the clock frequency
It only occurs during transitions
drills.why: Dynamic power is paid per transition and stops when the clock stops. Static power is the leakage of every transistor all the time, which is why a chip that is idle still has to be cooled.
